Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NextGen Renewables Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NextGen Renewables Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Development Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Casey Nguyen, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Riley Thompson, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. NextGen Renewables delivered exceptional results in the Q3 2024, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance. First, the profound impact of government incentives and subsidies, which fueled a significant portion of our EBITDA growth. Second, securing substantial new power purchase agreements at strong average pricing. Third, the expansion of our operating capacity and impressive generation output. Fourth, outstanding capacity factor performance across our solar, wind, and storage technologies. Fifth, our prudent management of debt levels and low financing costs. Sixth, continued positive trends in gross and operating margins. And seventh, excellent progress on construction projects with firm commercial operation dates on the horizon.

These achievements position us strongly for the future. Now, I'll hand over the call to Jordan Lee to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our financial performance in the Q3 2024 was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.85 billion, representing a 42% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $320 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $245 million, or $1.12 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

As we dive deeper into the financials, let me elaborate on some of those key aspects Alex mentioned, starting with the critical role of government incentives and subsidies. In our industry, these aren't mere tailwinds—they're essential accelerators pushing us toward widespread adoption. For NextGen Renewables, they contributed to a 22% year-over-year rise in adjusted EBITDA, making up about 18% of our total EBITDA this quarter, up from 14% last year. Let's unpack this with specifics on value capture, regional variations, and our proactive strategies.

At a high level, the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act stands out, with its flexible ITC and PTC structures. We've layered on domestic content bonuses and energy community adders, achieving effective rates of 50-70% on eligible projects. Our 1.2 GW of utility-scale solar-plus-storage assets ended the quarter with an average 42% ITC capture, yielding $285 million in tax equity proceeds—covering 60% of EPC costs. This lowers our WACC by 150 basis points to 5.8% and drops LCOE from $32/MWh unsubsidized to $18/MWh after incentives.

Pre-IRA, solar LCOE was around $42/MWh with a basic 26% ITC; now, our bifacial PERC modules with N-type TOPCon upgrades at 22.5% efficiency qualify for 30% ITC plus 10% domestic adder. We've sourced 85% U.S. components from partners like Nextracker and Array Technologies. For storage, our 400 MWh BESS under PPAs with California utilities like PG&E nets 30% ITC plus prevailing wage bonuses, nearly eliminating upfront costs.

Subsidies are shifting to spur innovation, like our 50 MW green hydrogen electrolyzer in Texas under the 45V PTC at $3.00/kg through 2027, securing a 15-year deal with Air Products at 85% capacity factor. Globally, module prices fell 45% YTD to $0.22/Wp, aided by U.S. tariffs, while incentives support pilots like perovskite tandems with Oxford PV targeting 28% efficiency by 2026.

In the U.S., IRA boom grew our backlog 35% to 4.5 GW, 70% credit-eligible; Section 45X yielded $42 million from our South Carolina fab, boosting margins. We're 95% compliant with FEOC rules. Europe sees REPowerEU and Net-Zero Act action: our 800 MW Dutch offshore wind stake gets 40% capex subsidy from the Innovation Fund, hitting €45/MWh LCOE. But phase-outs like Germany's EEG caps push us to 60% contracted revenue via corporate PPAs for CBAM compliance.

Asia varies: China's subsidies drive oversupply but low costs; India's PLI gave us 1 GW solar with 20% grants, lifting IRR to 14%; Brazil's auctions offer unsubsidized $36/MWh inflation-linked deals.

We're proactive with our Incentive Optimization Playbook, stacking 15 programs—like California SGIP, NY-Sun, Texas CREZ—for 28% NPV uplift on a 300 MW Texas solar farm. Our $200 million tax equity fund with Blackstone unlocks liquidity for H2 and storage R&D.

Risks include policy shifts potentially cutting 5-7% from 2025 EBITDA, but our $1.2 billion revolver and 2.5x debt/EBITDA headroom protect us. Incentives anchor FY24 guidance of $1.8-2.0 billion revenue, 25% margins, with $400 million credits in 2025 fueling 20% backlog growth. Cumulative value since IRA: $520 million.

Next, a major growth driver: our PPA execution. We secured 1.2 GW of new PPAs in the Americas and Europe—our best quarter since early 2022—bringing trailing 12-month bookings to 3.8 GW, on pace for 4.5-5 GW annually.

In the U.S. (75% or 900 MW): 400 MW solar-plus-storage with a hyperscaler in CAISO at $42/MWh (15-year), using 200 MW/800 MWh LFP BESS for peaks; 300 MW onshore wind in ERCOT at $38/MWh (12-year) with GE Vernova turbines and wake steering; 200 MW distributed solar in PJM/MISO at $45/MWh (10-year CPI-escalated).

Europe (300 MW): 200 MW offshore wind in UK North Sea at €55/MWh (~$60/MWh, 20-year CfD); 100 MW solar in Spain at €52/MWh with agrivoltaics.

Blended new PPA price: $41/MWh, +12% YoY, due to higher WACC (5.8-6.2%), IRA adders, and merchant spikes. Portfolio average: $39.50/MWh on 12 GW backlog (14-year tenor). We're pushing PPA-plus with merchant upside and 1 GW BESS for arbitrage ($5-8/MWh extra).

Ahead, 8 GW pipeline 65% contracted; LOIs for 500 MW from tech firms. U.S. to 60% capex, Europe 25%, Australia pilots.

These underpin 15-18% ROIC in BNEF's $1.2 trillion buildout.

On debt and financing: Total gross debt $5.2 billion (-8% YoY), net $4.35 billion (3.4x net debt/EBITDA, target 3-4x). 75% fixed-rate, 6.8-year maturity. Senior notes 45% ($2.35B, green bonds at 3.25%); term/project debt 30% ($1.56B); RCF undrawn $750M.

Blended cost 4.15% (-85 bps YoY): Refinanced $800M to SOFR+140bps, saving $45M/year; IRA tax equity $650M YTD dilutes WACC. Interest $128M (22% EBITDA).

U.S. sub-4% for hybrids; Europe 3.1% green bonds; APAC 2.8% Samurai. $1.8B maturities pre-funded; A-/BBB+ ratings. Targeting <3.0x leverage by 2025.

Gross margins hit 28.5% non-GAAP (+430 bps YoY), 31.2% GAAP. Polysilicon <$8/kg cut BOM to $0.22/Wp; TOPCon 65% mix at $0.28/Wp ASP. ESS 35.2%. U.S. 32.8% (45X credits); Europe 27.1%; APAC 26.4%.

Op margins 12.3% non-GAAP (+460 bps YoY), OpEx 16.2% revenue. R&D $45M (4.2%). Guide 11-13% FY. Q4 trough 27-29%, FY25 30%+ with HJT/ESS scale.

These trends reflect IRA tailwinds, supply deflation, mix shift.

I'll now turn the call over to Taylor Kim to discuss our project development activities.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 12 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

As part of this, let me update on construction progress and CODs across solar, wind, and BESS. We're set to commission 1.8 GW by end-2025, +25% YoY in CIP backlog, fueled by hyperscaler and utility PPAs.

Southwest Solar Portfolio (1.2 GWdc AZ/NV): Rattlesnake Valley 450 MWdc at 92% complete—modules 100%, inverters 85%. First 150 MW energize Q4 2024, full COD Q4. $420M capex (88% budget), IRA ITC.

Texas Panhandle Wind (600 MW): Lone Star II 300 MW at 78%—towers 65%, cabling 95%. COD Q1 2025 (slight slip), $550M under budget, PTC $28/MWh.

California BESS Cluster (400 MW/1.6 GWh): Sierra Peak 88% mechanical, COD H2 2025.

India Rajasthan 500 MWp 72%, COD Q3 2025; Europe floating PV 200 MW 55%, H1 2026.

40% hybrids; FID on 300 MW BESS add-ons. 2.5 GW 2025 CODs for 30% EBITDA growth.

Morgan Patel, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Morgan Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. We are dedicated to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing advanced technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. To tie into our performance, our capacity factors reflect this: fleet average 34.2% (+180 bps YoY), beating NREL by 250-400 bps.

Solar PV 29.1% (12.5 GW, +210 bps): TOPCon/trackers; Southwest 32.4%, AI soiling mitigation; Southeast 26.8%. Perovskite pilots for +5-7%.

Wind 42.1% blended (18.2 GW): Onshore 39.7% (Vestas 15 MW, WindOS -28% downtime); offshore 53.2% (Siemens Gamesa, LiDAR). Hybrids uplift EBITDA 15%.

Storage utilization 28.6%, RTE 92.4% (8.4 GW/32 GWh LFP): CAISO 35.2% ($120/kW-yr), ML optimization. Cell-to-pack cuts costs 15%.

Aurora AI boosts net CF 3%. FY24 guide 35-36%, $2.2-2.4B CAFD.

We believe that these technologies will play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

Next, Casey Nguyen will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Casey Nguyen:
Thank you, Morgan. Sustainability is a core value at NextGen Renewables, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability.

Now, Riley Thompson will provide operational highlights.

Riley Thompson:
Thank you, Casey. Our operational performance remains strong. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. On operating capacity, we hit a record 7.8 GW end-Q3 (+28% YoY, +8% QoQ), from 850 MW commissions: Prairie Winds III 450 MW wind (ERCOT, Vestas), SolarForge Nevada 300 MWdc (TOPCon), BatteryForge East 100 MW/400 MWh.

Mix: 52% wind (4.1 GW), 38% solar (3.0 GWdc), 10% storage (780 MW/2.8 GWh). NA 65%, Europe 28%, APAC 7%.

Generation: 5.2 TWh (+22% YoY, +12% QoQ), 38.4% CF. Wind 2.9 TWh (42.1%), solar 1.8 TWh (25.6%), storage 0.5 TWh equiv. (92% RTE). Curtailment <2%, AI forecasting.

O&M $18/kW-year; digital twins extend life 10%. Q3 guide 8.2 GW, 5.6-5.9 TWh.

We are implementing best practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.

I'll turn it back to Alex for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Riley. To summarize, NextGen Renewables had an exceptional Q3 2024. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our focus on sustainability will drive continued growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks for the question, John. International expansion is a key pillar of our growth strategy, balancing our strong U.S. foundation with opportunities abroad. We're targeting 30% of our capex outside North America over the next three years, focusing on Europe and Asia-Pacific where policy support and demand align with our strengths.

In Europe, we're ramping to 25% of development via REPowerEU and Net-Zero Industry Act. Our 800 MW offshore stake in Dutch Borssele benefits from €13 billion Innovation Fund subsidies, and we've hedged EEG phase-outs with corporate PPAs from tech leaders pursuing CBAM compliance. Recent PPA wins like 200 MW UK offshore at €55/MWh and 100 MW Spanish agrivoltaics underscore momentum—we see 2 GW added by 2026.

Asia-Pacific is bifurcated but promising: India's PLI secured 1 GW solar with 14% IRR uplift; Brazil's Proinfa auctions lock 20-year $36/MWh deals; Australia's NEM pilots 150-550 MW hybrids for FCAS premiums. China's supply supports imports at stable ASPs, but we're localizing in Pune for 50 GW auctions.

Challenges like grid queues (PJM 4 years) are pushing diversification—our 8 GW late-stage pipeline has early auction wins in Germany. We'll fund via green bonds and tax equity, maintaining leverage discipline. This positions us for global $1.2T buildout, with international ROIC matching U.S. 15-18%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Morgan Patel:
Great question, Jane—intermittency is core to our value prop, and we're tackling it head-on through tech integration and hybrids. Our 10% storage fleet (780 MW/2.8 GWh, scaling to 8.4 GW/32 GWh) delivers firming: CAISO BESS utilization 35.2% shaves duck curves, ERCOT arbitrage captures $200/MWh peaks. RTE 92.4%, degradation <1.2% with LFP from CATL/BYD.

Hybrids now 40-70% of pipeline—solar-plus-storage, wind-solar-BESS—boost dispatchability to 60%, minimizing clipping/curtailment to 1-2%. AI like Aurora suite and WindOS optimizes via AWS/The Weather Co forecasting, VPP bidding, LiDAR wake steering (+5-7% AEP).

Next-gen: long-duration iron-air pilots, perovskite tandems for higher base CFs (solar to 29%+), dispatchable solar thermal 100 MW pipeline. PPAs reflect this—'PPA-plus' shares merchant upside.

We've cut curtailment 15% fleet-wide, outperforming amid constraints. With IRA storage ITC and EU mandates, we're guiding 28.6% utilization uplift, turning intermittency into revenue convexity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Bob Johnson:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Jordan Lee:
Absolutely, Bob—subsidies are transformative for profitability, contributing 18% of Q3 EBITDA (+4% YoY). IRA ITC/PTC stack to 50-70%, dropping LCOE $32 to $18/MWh, WACC to 5.8%, $285M tax equity on 1.2 GW solar-storage. Section 45X $42M from SC fab; 45V H2 PTC de-risks $3/kg offtake.

Europe: 40% capex grants on offshore; Asia: India 20% PLI, Brazil unsub but take-or-pay. Our Playbook yields 28% NPV uplift, $520M cumulative value.

Profitability direct: gross margins 28.5-31.2%, op 12.3-14.1%. But risks—policy repeal could shave 5-7% 2025 EBITDA; mitigated by $1.2B revolver, diversification (U.S. 60%, Europe 25%). FY25 $400M credits fuel 25% margins amid capex deflation (wind $800/kW, storage $120/kWh).

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alice Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alice Lee:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Alice. We're bullish on demand growth, projecting 4-5% CAGR globally through 2030, driven by electrification, data centers, and industry. U.S. EIA sees 45 GW data center load by 2030; hyperscalers like Google/Microsoft chase 24/7 CFR, fueling our 3.8 GW TTM PPAs.

Tight grids—CAISO/ERCOT peaks, NEM reverse flows—boost ancillary premiums. Electrification adds 1-2% annual; AI hyperscalers 15-20% of new U.S. demand.

Our positioning: 12 GW contracted backlog at $39.50/MWh, hybrids for firming, 7.8 GW operating ramping output 22% YoY. Backlog to 15 GW construction-ready, targeting 10 GW operating by 2025. Merchant dislocation (ERCOT $200/MWh) aids pricing power.

Overall, $1.7T renewables TAM per BNEF; we're capturing via firm renewables, positioning for sustained growth.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of NextGen Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
